final_writeup:
The general FP claim remains unresolved, but the radius-one problem admits a useful exact normal form. A positive output is precisely a partition of G into triples spanning at least two edges; the missing edges can then be added as a matching. A negative output never needs edge additions: they can be discarded, leaving only a matching deletion.

This yields several polynomial branches. Greedily remove triples centered at a vertex having two remaining neighbors. If no vertices remain, this constructs a positive output. The remainder R always induces a matching; when |R|>n/3, deleting its edges makes R an independent set too large for any triangle partition. Thus only the regime 0<|R|≤n/3 survives this elementary algorithm. It follows in particular that every instance with n≤6 is solvable.

There are broader negative branches. A matching deletion followed by a modulo-three separator obstruction in the triangle-support graph certifies nonexistence. Also, if fewer than n/3 vertices have degree at least four, a locally maximal cut of the remaining subcubic graph supplies a matching deletion after which those high-degree vertices form a triangle cover too small for a partition. On the dense side, a bipartite matching condition for the vertices having at least two nonneighbors constructs a positive output.

These branches do not exhaust all graphs. The connected family W_a in the results has no nearby positive instance, has no large dissociation-set obstruction, and cannot be made triangle-free by a matching deletion; its negative answer instead follows from a one-vertex modulo-three separator. Hence both the tempting “P3-factor versus large dissociation set” dichotomy and the narrower “positive factor versus triangle-free matching deletion” strategy are false. No claim of full membership or hardness is made.

results.claim: A graph G has a radius-one neighbor with a triangle partition if and only if V(G) has a partition into triples each spanning at least two edges of G; moreover, a positive output may use additions only.
results.proof_sketch: The symmetric-difference graph of any radius-one edit has maximum degree one and hence is a matching. In a triangle of the output H, at most one of its three edges can be absent from G, since two missing edges in a triple share a vertex. Thus every partition triple spans at least two G-edges. Conversely, given such a partition, add the unique missing edge of each deficient triple. These added edges lie in vertex-disjoint triples, so they form a matching, and the resulting graph has the displayed triangle partition.

results.claim: Every radius-one negative output can be replaced by one obtained solely by deleting a matching from G.
results.proof_sketch: Write the edits producing a negative graph H as deleted edges D⊆E(G) and added edges A. Both are contained in one matching. Set H0=G-D=H-A. Then H0 is a subgraph of H, so a triangle partition of H0 would also be one of H. Hence H0 has none, while D remains a matching and dist_Δ(G,H0)≤1.

results.claim: There is a polynomially checkable modulo-three separator certificate for negative outputs.
results.proof_sketch: For a graph H, let T(H) have the same vertices and exactly the edges lying in at least one H-triangle. Let X⊆V and let q be the number of components of T(H)-X whose orders are nonzero modulo three. If H had a triangle partition, each such component would require a partition triangle meeting both it and X. A triangle cannot meet two different components of T(H)-X: the edge between its two non-X vertices would itself lie in T(H). The required crossing triangles are disjoint and consume distinct vertices of X, so q≤|X|. Thus q>|X| proves that H has no triangle partition. Given a matching deletion D, H=G-D, X, and q are all checkable in polynomial time.

results.claim: If S⊆V satisfies |S|>n/3 and Δ(G[S])≤1, then a valid negative output is constructible in polynomial time from S.
results.proof_sketch: The edges of G[S] form a matching D. Delete all of them and call the result H. Now S is independent in H. Every H-triangle contains at most one vertex of S, so n/3 vertex-disjoint triangles cover at most n/3 vertices of S, fewer than |S|. Therefore H has no triangle partition and dist_Δ(G,H)≤1.

results.claim: A greedy polynomial algorithm resolves every input except possibly when it leaves between 1 and n/3 vertices.
results.proof_sketch: Repeatedly choose a remaining vertex with two remaining neighbors and remove it together with two such neighbors. The removed triples span at least two G-edges. At termination the remainder R has maximum degree at most one. If R is empty, add the missing edge in every deficient removed triple, giving a positive output. If |R|>n/3, apply the preceding independent-set construction to R. Hence the only unresolved outcome is 0<|R|≤n/3.

results.claim: Given X with |X|<n/3 and Δ(G-X)≤3, a valid negative output can be constructed in polynomial time. Consequently this applies whenever fewer than n/3 vertices of G have degree at least four.
results.proof_sketch: Find a cut of G-X locally maximal under single-vertex flips. At such a cut every vertex has at most as many same-side as opposite-side neighbors, hence at most one same-side neighbor because its residual degree is at most three. The monochromatic edges form a matching D. In H=G-D, H-X is bipartite and therefore triangle-free. Thus every H-triangle meets X, but n/3 disjoint triangles would require at least n/3 distinct vertices of X. For the corollary, take X to be all vertices whose G-degree is at least four.

results.claim: There is a polynomially recognizable dense-side condition producing a positive output.
results.proof_sketch: Let C={v:d_complement(G)(v)≥2}, L=V\C, and m=n/3. Suppose |C|≤m and the bipartite graph G[C,L] has a matching saturating two clones of every c∈C. Group each c with its two distinct matched neighbors; every such triple spans two edges centered at c. The unused part of L has size 3(m-|C|). Since every vertex of L has at most one nonneighbor, any arbitrary triple of unused L misses at most one G-edge. These triples form the required factor. Saturation is testable by ordinary bipartite matching, after which the missing edges are added as a matching.

results.claim: The complete target is solvable for n=0,3,6.
results.proof_sketch: For n=0 return the empty partition. Otherwise run the greedy algorithm above. Its remainder has size divisible by three. For n=3 or 6, a nonempty remainder therefore has size at least three, which is strictly greater than n/3; this invokes the negative branch. An empty remainder invokes the positive branch. All constructions are polynomial and respect radius one.

results.claim: For every integer a≥2 there is a connected, triangle-support-connected graph W_a of order 3(5a+2) having no P3/triangle factor although its largest induced subgraph of maximum degree one has only 10<n/3 vertices.
results.proof_sketch: Let W_a consist of a vertex z and five pairwise anticomplete cliques C_i of size 3a+1, with z adjacent to every clique vertex. A good triple not containing z must lie wholly in one C_i: a triple crossing cliques spans at most one edge. The unique factor triple containing z touches at most two cliques, leaving at least three entire C_i to be covered internally, impossible because |C_i|≡1 mod 3. For the dissociation number, a set containing z has size at most two, while a set avoiding z contains at most two vertices of each clique. Choosing two per clique attains 10. Every edge lies in a triangle, so the triangle-support graph is connected.

results.claim: The family W_a also shows that restricting the negative branch to making the graph triangle-free by a matching deletion is insufficient, while the separator certificate detects its negative answer.
results.proof_sketch: Each C_i has at least seven vertices. Removing a matching from a clique of that size leaves a triangle: choose three vertices no two of which form a deleted pair. Hence no matching deletion makes W_a triangle-free. Nevertheless take X={z}. The graph T(W_a)-X has five components, all of order 3a+1, so q=5>|X|=1. The separator criterion therefore correctly certifies that W_a itself has no triangle partition.
